# Migrations

This project has **two** migration tracks. Both must run.

## 1. `drizzle/*.sql` — generated by drizzle-kit

Produced by `drizzle-kit generate` from `lib/database/schema.ts`, tracked in
`drizzle/meta/_journal.json`, applied by `drizzle-kit migrate`.

The lineage here was squashed to a single `0000_baseline` on 2026-08-19. Before
that there were two competing `0000_*` baselines and two journals (the second a
macOS duplicate-file artifact, `_journal 3.json`), which made `drizzle-kit
generate` fail outright with a parent-snapshot collision. The superseded
lineage is in git history if it is ever needed.

## 2. `drizzle/migrations/*.sql` — hand-written

**drizzle-kit does not know these exist.** They are applied by
`scripts/apply-sql-migrations.ts` and tracked by name and checksum in
`public.__sql_migrations`.

This track exists for things drizzle's schema does not model — chiefly RLS
policies — and for data backfills.

### Why the tracking was added

For eight months nothing executed this directory. `2025-12-02_add_contact_source.sql`
added `contact_submissions.source`; the application began writing that column the
same day; the column did not exist; every insert threw; and the handler caught
the error and carried on sending the email. The result was a contact form that
appeared to work while silently storing nothing. Six test rows from December 2025
were the entire contents of that table.

If you write SQL here, it does not run until you run it.

## Commands

    npm run db:migrate         # both tracks
    npm run db:migrate:status  # what is pending in track 2

`--baseline` records files as applied without executing them. It was used once,
on 2026-08-19, to adopt tracking on a database whose migrations had been applied
by hand. The old files cannot be re-run — `2025-11-11_add_show_slug.sql`
references a `name` column that a later migration dropped.

`*.rollback.sql` files are never applied automatically.

## Known pending

As of 2026-10-04, nothing from #51 is applied. In order:

1. **Track 1** `0001_pieces_and_drop_length_seconds.sql`: creates `pieces` and
   `arrangement_pieces`, drops `shows.length_seconds` (0 of 22 rows set, no code
   reads it).
2. **Track 2**, all pending:
   - `2026-08-23_trim_title_whitespace.sql` (from #43, still unapplied).
   - `2026-10-04_arrangement_type_into_scene.sql`: copies `arrangements.type`
     into `scene` where `scene` is null, then drops `type`. Replaces
     `2025-11-11_remove_arrangement_type.sql`, which was never applied and
     dropped the column without copying. The 3 rows with `type` set already
     have a matching `scene`, so the copy touches nothing today; it stops
     with an error if a value does not map or disagrees. The 3 arrangements
     with no scene at all (51, 53, 58) are #49 and are not touched.
   - `2026-10-04_delete_placeholder_tag.sql`: deletes tag id 1 `'tag'` only
     if no show or arrangement uses it (none did on 2026-10-04).
   - `2026-10-04_pieces_rls.sql`: staff-only RLS on the two new tables. Needs
     track 1 first.

**Before the first `drizzle-kit migrate` against production:**
`drizzle.__drizzle_migrations` still holds the three rows of the pre-squash
lineage (latest `created_at` 1755921791974). drizzle-kit applies every journal
entry newer than the latest row, so it would try to run `0000_baseline` and
fail on `CREATE TYPE ... already exists`. Record the baseline as applied
first:

    insert into drizzle.__drizzle_migrations (hash, created_at)
    values ('3bda43589e3a583326c53611d0657e5c5d7bbd85b6526d00bc62f82ae06bcb7f', 1787193232973);

The hash is `sha256` of `drizzle/0000_baseline.sql`; `created_at` is its
`when` in `meta/_journal.json`.
